The Nuevo Laredo Zoo will offer a night of tradition, entertainment and family togetherness on Friday, Oct. 30, with a special Día de Muertos celebration featuring themed decorations, children's activities and interactions with some of its animals, according to CML Noticias.

The event runs from 7 to 9 p.m., with completely free admission for children and adults, the zoo's administration said.

Visitors will be able to walk through spaces decorated with murals, altars and photo settings inspired by Mexican traditions, according to the report. Attractions include a catrín set at the main roundabout, a monarch butterfly decoration in front of the administrative offices and a xoloitzcuintle mural in the Serengeti area.

A cemetery-themed decoration will be set up on the Serengeti esplanade, an altar of the dead behind the marmoset area and a sugar-skull mural on the giraffe bridge, the report said. In Kangaroo Plaza there will be a stage decorated with a guitar.

For children, a seasonal movie will be shown at 7 p.m. in the theater in front of the aviary, where popcorn and juices will be offered, according to CML Noticias. Educational tables will also be set up in front of the dromedary area, with activities to help children learn about Día de Muertos.

The program includes a capybara interaction at 7 p.m. and a giraffe activity at 8 p.m., when enrichment activities for lemurs and marmosets will also take place, focused on their behavior and care, the report said. Zoo and Aquarium director Daniel Del Fierro Cárdenas said the activities aim to combine fun with learning and closeness to animal life.

Entry is through the Nuevo Laredo Zoo ticket office on Luis Donaldo Colosio Boulevard in the Viveros neighborhood, and information is available at 867 714 5423, according to the report.

Sources:

  • CML Noticias, “Celebrará Zoológico de Nuevo Laredo el Día de Muertos con actividades gratuitas,” Oct. 29, 2026

title: Nuevo Laredo Zoo to host free Día de Muertos night Oct. 30 with kids' activities and animal encounters
